summary.verdict: The science on this page is at winner level and the presentation is not there yet. The 9-23 falsification chain, the apo control used to retire a claim, and the pH comparison with one variable changed would each score well on the Best Model ballot, and every number in the prose reconciles with the nine run reports. What a judge meets first is a definition of molecular dynamics, four folded results with no run list, seven figures with no captions, three undefined metrics, and the strongest finding of the nine runs folded inside a summary section.
strengths: The 9-23 falsification chain: a hypothesis, a construct built to discriminate, the measurement that refuses it at 0.0% of frames, a different mechanism found, and the next experiment named. Nothing in the six Best Model winners we read is this clean.
Event-level reporting instead of a mean: the bidentate bridge 'broke 94 times or 22.9% of the trajectory', with each break bounded at 0.68 ns.
The apo receptor run used as a noise floor, and a claim the project would have liked then withdrawn because the floor will not carry it.
Correlations reported with the n they rest on and the caveat attached, including the +0.71 contact-count figure called 'strongly influenced by individual constructs'.
Compute cost disclosed: 270 ns of production dynamics and 25.9 GPU-hours on a named GPU. Only one of the six winners discusses compute at all, and without numbers.
priorities: Write the abstract sheet. It is empty. It is the first thing a judge reads, and every other dry lab page we review has one.

Give the histidine-tag result its own numbered section, and add a run list at the top of Key findings. Correct the run list first: your 12 October overview counts a K18R simulation among the nine and no K18R run exists, the ninth system is the AtPEP1 7-23 benchmark.

Define clamp integrity, bidentate Arg487 occupancy and the acceptance gate at first use, and label the distance-only and the distance-plus-angle criteria at every number that uses them. The tagged construct reads as 2.4% in the table and as zero in the prose.
Settle where the purification tag sits and what the conserved window is. Three pages in this cluster currently give different answers to both.

Caption, number and cite the seven figures, and publish the reuse material: engine and version, thermostat, barostat, ions, box, the seed value, the nine run reports, the analysis code, and n equals 1 on the table.

ballot.question: How impressive is the modeling or computational approach?
ballot.note: Nine all-atom systems with one variable changed at a time is strong work, and the page gives no orientation paragraph, no simulation engine and no spread on any number, which is what this question reads first.

ballot.question: Did the model or computational approach help the team understand, predict, or design a part, device, or system?
ballot.where: 2. Key findings and design implications, and 10. Application of results
ballot.note: The tag moved off the C terminus before expression, pH 5.5 became the default condition, and K18R dropped to a hypothesis. The verbs need to be yours and past tense wherever these are reported.

ballot.question: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?
ballot.note: The AtPEP1 7-23 benchmark and the apo control are real external checks, and the published hotspot list is used as a third. No bench measurement appears anywhere on the page, and the single seed is admitted only in Limitations.

ballot.question: Does the modeling or computational approach provide a good example for others?
ballot.note: No engine or version, no input files, no seed, no run reports and no code. Three metrics carry every number and none is defined, and the seven figures have no captions or numbers.

winners: A lead of 100 to 400 words: the problem, the cost of answering it at the bench, the model named and given a job, and what it takes in and gives out
A scope or assumptions declaration near the top
Methods before results, with tool choices justified and not only listed
Results in blocks, each block ending in a stated consequence
A comparison against data the model did not already contain
skeleton.gap: From section 3 onward our order matches the winners and our blocks do end in consequences, which is the hard part. The gap is at the top and in the apparatus: no abstract sheet, no run list, a lead that defines molecular dynamics instead of naming the question, and no scope statement. One block is also missing, since the histidine-tag run is the only one of the nine without a section of its own.

extras: The abstract sheet for this page is empty, so this review carries no notes on it. Write it: the design question, the nine runs, the tag finding, and the two limits of 30 ns and one seed.

The histidine-tag fold says the six histidines are 'beginning at Asn23'. Limitations says 'Adding six histidines C-terminal to Asn23', and the table gives the tagged construct 29 residues, so the histidines are positions 24 to 29. Use the Limitations wording in both places.
'AtPep1' appears nine times on this page and 'AtPEP1' four times. The Methodology page uses 'AtPEP1' twenty-seven times and never 'AtPep1'. Standardise on AtPEP1 across the cluster.
Construct names mix hyphens and en dashes: '9-23' sixteen times and '9–23' six times, and the same for 7-23 and 15-23. Pick one and use it in the headings too.
'behaviours' in section 4 and 'behavior' in sections 6 and 7. Pick one spelling for the page.
Section 10's first subheading is 'Wetlab'. The rest of the wiki says 'wet lab'.
Section 2 has 'at distances between 2.55 and 9.37 Å , this is not the short-distance interaction', with a space before the comma.

Section 4 says 'In the nine-residue construct, its occupancy increases from 53.7% to 90.1%'. Constructs are named by residue range everywhere else on the page, so write '15-23' and keep the residue count in brackets if it is useful.

Section 4's 'We found that the eight N-terminal residues had an average fluctuation above 2 Å' can be read two ways. Say whether each of the eight was above 2 Å or whether the eight averaged above it.
Section 5 says the 9-23 bridge 'transiently dissociated multiple times' and then gives the count as 94. Delete 'multiple times' and keep the number.

notes.anchor: Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation is a fundamental computational methodology
notes.title: Open with the question, not the definition
notes.body: Your first two sentences define MD for a reader who has to reach the third one to learn why the page exists. The winners open with the problem, what it costs to answer at the bench, the method named with a job, and what goes in and comes out. Keep your definition and put it after that.
notes.after: Docking gave us one pose for BoPEP4 in the PEPR1 groove and no way to tell whether it holds. Testing every variant at the bench would cost [number] weeks, so we ran nine all-atom trajectories of 30 ns each and asked which contacts survive. MD integrates Newtonian equations of motion and tracks positions and interactions over time, which is what lets us watch a pose come apart.
notes.excerpt_note: Four sentences: the biology, what trial and error costs at the bench, then the model named and given a job.
notes.ballot: How impressive is the modeling or computational approach?

notes.anchor: We applied this to our project to understand the translation and secretion efficiency
notes.title: This page did not study secretion
notes.body: The nine runs ask whether a docked BoPEP4 pose holds its grip on the PEPR1 ectodomain. They say nothing about translation or secretion, and one receptor was simulated, so 'the interactions between different receptors' describes work that is not on this page. This paragraph is also the whole of section 5 on the Methodology page, word for word, so correct it in one place and link to it from the other.
notes.after: We used MD to ask whether our docked poses of BoPEP4 on the PEPR1 ectodomain hold up once the atoms are free to move.

notes.anchor: Rather than treating a single docking pose as a definitive representation
notes.title: You name what docking could not settle
notes.body: This clause states the limit of the step before it, which is what makes the whole page necessary. You treat the docking pose as a prediction that still has to be tested, and you say so before any result arrives. A judge who reads only this sentence knows what the nine runs were for.

notes.anchor: While MD runs can answer crucial hypotheses, they can also serve as trigger points
notes.title: Cut this line or make it concrete
notes.body: 'Trigger points for unique, project-altering strategies' promises something the sentence does not deliver, and you already have the real example a few lines below. Name it here and delete the rest.
notes.after: One of these runs changed a design decision before expression: the purification tag moved off the C terminus.

notes.anchor: Key findings and design implications
notes.title: Add the run list before the findings
notes.body: A judge meets four folded results before learning that nine systems were simulated or what each one was for. Your own 12 October document has the overview paragraph this page needs at the top. Correct its run list first: it counts a K18R simulation among the nine and no K18R run exists, the ninth system is the AtPEP1 7-23 benchmark. Two smaller things to settle here as well: the folds run in a different order from sections 4 to 7, and the apo control has no fold at all.
notes.after: Nine systems were simulated: full-length BoPEP4 as the reference, the AtPEP1 7-23 benchmark, three truncations at 7-23, 9-23 and 15-23, the C-terminally tagged construct, full length and 9-23 again at pH 5.5, and the receptor with no peptide as a control. [One clause per run saying what it was for.]
notes.excerpt_note: Three sentences name what was modelled and at what scales, then hand over to the parts list.
notes.ballot: How impressive is the modeling or computational approach?

notes.anchor: The decision to move the purification tag to the C-terminus resulted in six histidines
notes.title: Give the tag result its own section
notes.body: This is the strongest result your MD work produced and the only one of the nine runs without a section of its own. It sits folded inside Key findings at about 290 words of 5,045, between two other folds. Promote it to a numbered section ahead of Wild type, name the construct, and say who acted on it and when.
notes.excerpt_note: The verdict on the batch gets its own short sentence instead of being folded into a clause.
notes.ballot: Did the model or computational approach help the team understand, predict, or design a part, device, or system?

notes.anchor: a more rigorous test considering both distance and bond angle showed that the bidentate salt bridge was missing
notes.title: Label the two criteria at every number
notes.body: The table gives the tagged construct 2.4% bidentate occupancy and this sentence says the bridge was missing in every frame. Both are right under different tests, and a reader cannot tell that from the page. Name the two tests once, then attach the name to every number that uses them, in the table column and in section 8 as well.
notes.after: Under the distance-only test the bidentate bridge appears in 2.4% of frames. Under the stricter test, which requires the distance and the bond angle, it appears in no frame at all, against 100% of frames for the untagged peptide.
notes.excerpt_note: An apparent agreement is refused once the test behind it is examined, and a second check settles it.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: The difference in these findings indicates the tagged peptide fails to maintain the native salt bridge
notes.title: This sentence repeats the one before
notes.body: The sentence above already gives the result and the criterion the construct passed. This one states both again and adds nothing. Cut it so the design consequence lands immediately after the evidence.
notes.after: Delete this sentence. The design option in the next sentence then follows straight from the evidence.

notes.anchor: the bidentate salt bridge between peptide Glu12 and receptor His227 was present in 99.9% of frames
notes.title: Two interactions share one name
notes.body: Everywhere else on the page 'the bidentate salt bridge' means Asn23 with Arg487, and your table column is headed 'Bidentate Arg487'. Here the same phrase names Glu12 with His227, one fold below the Arg487 result. Section 6 calls this pair 'the interaction', which is the safer wording.
notes.after: At this pH, with His14, His22 and His227 protonated to reflect this environment, the contact between peptide Glu12 and receptor His227 was present in 99.9% of frames, against 0.8% at pH 7.0.

notes.anchor: We therefore found this to be the more suitable condition for studying BoPEP4
notes.title: You changed a default and kept the control
notes.body: One sentence names the decision this run produced and says the old condition was kept as a control. That is the shape a Best Model judge looks for: a condition chosen on evidence, with the comparison still on the table. The verb is past tense and the choice is yours.
notes.ballot: Did the model or computational approach help the team understand, predict, or design a part, device, or system?

notes.anchor: In the full-length peptide (Lys7–Arg156), a salt bridge between Lys7 and Asp129
notes.title: The full-length peptide is twenty-three residues
notes.body: Your own table gives the full-length system as residues 1 to 23. It cannot run from Lys7 to residue 156, and it does not begin at Lys7. Asp129 and Arg156 are receptor residues, so this bracket mixes the two numbering schemes a reader is already holding in mind.
notes.after: In the full-length peptide, residues 1 to 23, a salt bridge between peptide Lys7 and receptor Asp129 was present in 98.7% of frames at a distance of 2.81 Å.

notes.anchor: The simulation of wild-type BoPEP4 led us to re-examine the evidence for the planned K18R mutation
notes.title: This fold repeats section four
notes.body: The fold in section 4 gives the same three findings, the 53.7% occupancy, the 2.55 to 9.37 Å range and the Gly20 contact with Phe371, with the reasoning around them. Keep the result here in two sentences and leave the evidence where a reader can act on it.
notes.after: The wild-type run weakened the case for K18R. The Lys18 to Asp348 contact holds in only 53.7% of frames, and Phe371 spends most of the trajectory on Gly20, so K18R is now a hypothesis to be tested (section 4).

notes.anchor: Each trajectory 30 ns of production dynamics from a single random seed
notes.title: A verb is missing here
notes.body: This sentence has no verb, and it joins two separate facts with 'and'. Split it into two.
notes.after: Each trajectory ran 30 ns of production dynamics from a single random seed. We saved 1,500 frames from each one for analysis.

notes.anchor: The nine systems varied in four ways
notes.title: You fix the design of the experiment
notes.body: Four named variables, then one sentence saying everything else was held constant. That tells a judge which runs can be compared with which, before any result appears. It is a cheap sentence that does more structural work than anything else in this section.
notes.excerpt_note: Three bullets fix the scope of an 8,000-word page in about forty words.
notes.ballot: How impressive is the modeling or computational approach?

notes.anchor: The same analysis codebase was used for all nine trajectories
notes.title: Say which software, and publish the inputs
notes.body: The page never names the MD engine or its version. The Methodology page says the runs used OpenMM on Google Colab, while this page reports A100 hours, so a reader cannot tell what to install or where it ran. Add the engine and version, the thermostat, barostat, ion concentration and box size, the seed value, and links to the nine run reports and the analysis code.
notes.after: All nine systems were run in [engine, version] with [thermostat] and [barostat] at [temperature] and [pressure], neutralised with [ions] in a [box] box. The nine run reports and the analysis code are at [link], including the random seed used for each trajectory.
notes.excerpt_note: The hand-off is written for a stranger: what they supply, and what the pipeline then does on its own.
notes.ballot: Does the modeling or computational approach provide a good example for others?

notes.anchor: which allows for a common footing in analysis of structural stability
notes.title: Define the three metrics here
notes.body: Clamp integrity, bidentate Arg487 occupancy and the acceptance gate carry every number on this page, and none of them is defined anywhere in the cluster. Our judges read many pages a day and are not in our field. Define all three at the point where you claim the common footing, and say the gate was fixed before the runs started.
notes.after: The three reported metrics are defined once here. Clamp integrity is [definition]. Bidentate Arg487 occupancy is [definition]. A trajectory passes the acceptance gate if Asn23 stays within 4 Å of Arg487 in at least 60% of frames, a rule we fixed before any run started.
notes.ballot: Does the modeling or computational approach provide a good example for others?

notes.anchor: The nine trajectories: the four variables that change between them
notes.title: The table needs its caption and an n
notes.body: This caption is good and no sighted reader ever sees it, because the page source marks it visually hidden. Make it visible, number it, and add a line saying what the columns mean. Every value in the table also comes from one trajectory, so mark n equals 1 in the table itself. Your Limitations section says single-seed differences could be variance, and the table should not quietly disagree with it.
notes.excerpt_note: The spread is reported as a property of the trajectory, so a reader can see how much of each number to trust.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: This was consistent with the alanine scan results, which found that mutations to the first six residues
notes.title: The alanine scan started at residue six
notes.body: The scan on the Sprints page runs from S6A to N23A, so residues 1 to 5 were never substituted. What put the first six residues outside the contact region was the contact map: the Sprints page says 'the map putting residues 1 to 6 outside the contact region entirely'. Cite the map here, and keep the scan for the position it did test.
notes.after: This was consistent with the contact map, which puts residues 1 to 6 outside the contact region, and with the alanine scan, where S6A carried one of the smallest penalties of the positions tested.

notes.anchor: All residues past Pro10 had over 75% contact with the receptor, except for Pro19
notes.title: Point the reader at your figures
notes.body: The figure directly above this paragraph plots per-residue contact and fluctuation, which is what these three sentences list in words. It has no number, no visible caption and no sentence pointing to it, and the same is true of all seven figures on the page. The titles in the page source are already usable captions: 'Per-residue contact occupancy and fluctuation for the wild-type reference run' is one of them. Make them visible, number them, and cite each figure in the sentence it supports.
notes.after: All residues past Pro10 had over 75% contact with the receptor, except for Pro19 (Figure [n]).
notes.ballot: Does the modeling or computational approach provide a good example for others?

notes.anchor: Our conserved window 15-23, defined by aligning sequences from the PEP receptor family
notes.title: Our pages disagree on this window
notes.body: The Sprints page corrects this page by name: 'The conserved region stops at 20, not 23. We have been describing 15 to 23 as the conserved block.' It puts 21, 22 and 23 in the variable set. The alignment was also of PEP peptides, not of the receptor family, so the second half of the clause names the wrong sequences. Use one window across the cluster and say which alignment defined it.
notes.after: Residues 15 to 23 are the window we report contact over. The invariant block in the PEP peptide alignment is 15 to 20, with 21 to 23 variable (see Sprints and Results).

notes.anchor: Arg9 has a fluctuation of 1.32 Å and a mean closest approach of 2.79 Å and 100% contact
notes.title: Three numbers and an independent method
notes.body: One residue, three measurements, and then the docking result they explain. Two methods with no shared assumptions landing on Arg9 is better evidence than either on its own, and the sentence shows that without announcing it.
notes.excerpt_note: Two predictions of the simulation are each checked against a separate measurement, and the claim stays at direction of effect.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: so we did not pursue the Δ1 and Δ1-3 designs
notes.title: Expand the delta notation once
notes.body: A judge reading this page on its own cannot tell what Δ1 and Δ1-3 are. The Sprints page calls the same pair Δ1-2 and Δ1-3 in one place and Δ1 and Δ1-3 in another, so the names need settling too. Give the residue ranges here and use one name across the cluster.
notes.after: so we did not pursue the shallow N-terminal cuts, Δ1-3 (residues 4 to 23) and Δ1-[number], and opted for the deeper 7-23 and 9-23 truncations instead.

notes.anchor: Overall, the MD results provide a more specific basis for the K18R design
notes.title: The fold ends twice
notes.body: The paragraph two above already says K18R stays plausible, that the geometry is untested, and that a dedicated simulation is needed. This paragraph says all three again in four sentences. Keep the earlier version and let the fold end on the peptide-length result.
notes.after: Delete this paragraph. 'Whether K18R achieves this geometry remains untested and requires a dedicated simulation' already closes the argument.

notes.anchor: within the defined cutoff distance
notes.title: Fix the grammar and give the cutoff
notes.body: 'had the 81.1% of frames with the distance between Asn23 and Arg487 within the defined cutoff distance' does not parse, and the cutoff itself is not given until section 6, where it appears as 4 Å. Put the number here, at first use.
notes.after: Asn23 stayed within 4 Å of Arg487 in 81.1% of frames.

notes.anchor: We initially hypothesized that the unusual instability was caused by the novel N-terminus
notes.title: Split this paragraph into five
notes.body: This is one paragraph of about 450 words, and it carries the best argument on the page. A judge skimming it will miss the chain. Break it where the argument turns and leave your sentences as they are.
notes.after: End the first paragraph at 'forming a new interaction with the receptor'. Start the second at 'To investigate this possibility'. Start the third at 'In the 7-23 construct, the alpha-amino group of Lys7'. Start the fourth at 'The truncation series had revealed an unexpected N-terminal anchor'. Start the fifth at 'Directly testing the proposed role of Lys7'.

notes.anchor: the positively-charged alpha-ammonium group of Arg9 becomes the new N-terminal residue
notes.title: A group is not a residue
notes.body: A chemical group cannot become a residue. Arg9 becomes the new N-terminal residue, and it carries a free alpha-amino group. The page also calls this same group alpha-ammonium, alpha-amino and the Greek-letter form in three places, so choose one name and use it throughout.
notes.after: In the 9-23 construct, Arg9 becomes the new N-terminal residue, so it carries a positively charged free alpha-amino group that could form a new interaction with the receptor.

notes.anchor: the alpha-amino group of Lys7 was 7.11 Å away from its closest receptor carboxylate
notes.title: You print the number that kills your idea
notes.body: You proposed that a new terminal charge caused the instability, then simulated the construct that would separate the two explanations, and reported the result: 0.0% of frames inside 4 Å. The hypothesis is refused by a measurement built to discriminate, and the number is given in full. Hypothesis, discriminating construct, rejection, alternative mechanism, next experiment: no page in the six winners we read runs that chain this cleanly.
notes.excerpt_note: A negative result, the diagnosis behind it, the fix that would follow, and the admission that the fix is blocked too.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: This is also seen in the occupancy of the Lys7 contact, which reached 99.9% in the BoPEP4
notes.title: The same contact has two occupancies
notes.body: Earlier in this paragraph Lys7 to Asp129 is 98.7% in BoPEP4 and Lys7 'contributed' 19.0% in AtPep1. Here 'the occupancy of the Lys7 contact' is 99.9% and 23.5%. These are probably two different measures, one for a named atom pair and one for any receptor contact. Say which is which in both sentences, or a judge will read it as a contradiction.
notes.after: Lys7 holds [metric: any receptor contact] in 99.9% of BoPEP4 frames and 23.5% of AtPep1 frames, while the named Lys7 to Asp129 salt bridge holds in 98.7%. [Check which metric each number reports.]

notes.anchor: Unexpectedly, the peptide was highly organized throughout the simulation
notes.title: A control that refused to be negative
notes.body: You designed 15-23 to fail, it did not, and you say so in the second sentence instead of burying it. The paragraph then bounds the result: dissociation from an LRR ectodomain can take microseconds to milliseconds, so 30 ns of occupancy cannot speak to affinity. The claim that survives is stated last and it is the right size.
notes.excerpt_note: The mismatch, its candidate causes, the conclusion that survives it, and the accuracy the model actually needs.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: The proposed role of Lys7 still awaits experimental confirmation
notes.title: The same next step appears three times
notes.body: The same next step appears in the Key findings fold, at the end of the N-terminal anchor fold, and again here. Three statements of one experiment read as padding. Keep the fullest version, which is in the anchor fold, and cut this one to a cross-reference.
notes.after: The proposed role of Lys7 still awaits the full-length K7A simulation described above.

notes.anchor: Because conventional molecular dynamics does not dynamically simulate pH
notes.title: You state the method's limit first
notes.body: The paragraph names what the method cannot do, then what you did instead, then which three residues changed, then that nothing else changed. A reader knows exactly what 'pH 5.5' means here before any number arrives. The closing clause, that the three protonation changes are the only variable, is what makes the comparison that follows readable.
notes.excerpt_note: The assumption inside a borrowed method is written out in plain words, then the biology that breaks it is named.
notes.ballot: How impressive is the modeling or computational approach?

notes.anchor: At the same time, the trajectory does not support the proposed His14 pH-switch mechanism
notes.title: You retire your own mechanism
notes.body: In the same paragraph as a win, you report that the His14 switch your design proposed does not appear: about 6.1 Å from the nearest receptor carboxylate and 0.0% of frames inside 4 Å at either condition. Then you name the interaction that does respond to pH. Withdrawing your own proposal in the place a reader will look for it is the strongest credibility move available to this page.
notes.excerpt_note: One of the team's own top predicted targets is shown to be an artefact of the method, in the section where a reader will look.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: Therefore, the combined effect of truncation and protonation is important
notes.title: Lead with the finding, not its label
notes.body: 'Is important' asks the reader to wait for the point, and the point is in the next clause: neither condition alone broke the clamp and the two together did. Put that first and the three occupancies become evidence for a claim the reader already holds.
notes.after: Truncation and protonation only broke the clamp together. Neither alone produced the strong self-contact seen in the failed trajectory: truncation raised occupancy from 1.1% to 17.4% at neutral pH, protonation raised full-length occupancy to 64.7%, and only the combination reached 96.9%.

notes.anchor: Moreover, the 54 interface residues shifted by only +0.125
notes.title: One sentence carries four findings
notes.body: This runs to about sixty words and holds the interface comparison, the residue 41 to 55 difference and the rigidity of residue 738. Split it into short sentences. Say as well what 'shifted by' measures, because a reader cannot tell whether +0.125 Å is a difference in mean fluctuation or a displacement.
notes.after: The 54 interface residues differed from wild type by +0.125 Å in [metric], against +0.156 Å for the other 656 residues. The largest differences sit at residues 41 to 55, the N-terminal cap of the ectodomain. The final residue, 738, is the most rigid in the structure. Both are chain-end effects, far from the binding groove.

notes.anchor: the seven peptide-bound runs differed from one another by 0.59
notes.title: Seven here and eight in section eight
notes.body: Nine systems minus the apo control leaves eight peptide-bound runs, and section 8 says so: 'Across the eight peptide-containing runs'. The sentence above this one also quotes a 1.58 to 2.16 Å range across 'the peptide-bound runs'. If one run is left out of this particular comparison, name it and say why.

notes.anchor: Because changing the peptide produced more receptor-side variation than removing it entirely
notes.title: The control retires your own claim
notes.body: The apo run is used as a noise floor, and then a claim your project would have liked, that BoPEP4 stabilises PEPR1, is withdrawn because the floor will not carry it. One of the six winners runs a comparable baseline and none of them uses it to retire a claim. Repeat this sentence in Limitations, so a judge who reads only that section still sees it.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: In other words, overall structural stability was largely independent
notes.title: Move this sentence to the front
notes.body: This is the clearest sentence in the section and it is the last one. A judge from another field can carry it away, which four correlation coefficients cannot. Open the section with it and let the numbers follow as evidence.
notes.after: Overall structural stability was largely independent of whether the key binding interaction stayed chemically intact. Across the eight peptide-containing runs, backbone RMSD over the conserved window correlated only weakly with the bidentate Arg487 salt bridge, at +0.13 and +0.29, while correlations with clamp integrity were −0.03 and −0.07.

notes.anchor: illustrates how each peptide-peptide complex evolved during the simulation
notes.title: Peptide-peptide should be peptide-receptor
notes.body: There is no peptide-peptide complex in this work. The same sentence has it right eight words earlier. Fix the second one.
notes.after: While the 30 ns snapshot of each peptide-receptor complex illustrates how that complex evolved during the simulation, these timescales are too short to capture many protein-peptide dissociation events.

notes.anchor: Moreover, these results should be interpreted as the structural persistence
notes.title: The same caveat three times
notes.body: This paragraph says the 30 ns window cannot speak to binding strength in its first sentence, again two sentences later, and again here. One statement is enough, and the repetition weakens the sentence after it, which is the one that says what would be needed.
notes.after: Delete this sentence and keep the one that follows it.

notes.anchor: The absence of replicate simulations constrains the reliability of construct comparisons
notes.title: You say what one seed cannot support
notes.body: This paragraph names the limit, explains the mechanism behind it, and then says which of your own comparisons could be variance. That is the hardest thing on this page to write and you wrote it plainly. What it needs is for the notation elsewhere to agree with it, which is why the nine-system table should carry n equals 1.
notes.excerpt_note: The statistic is chosen because the sample is small, and n is stated in the same sentence as the result.
notes.ballot: Did the team use experimental or other relevant data to develop, train, or validate the model or computational approach?

notes.anchor: the results informed the decision to move the purification tag to the N-terminus
notes.title: Our pages disagree about the tag
notes.body: The Methodology page still specifies the old design in Phase 2: 'while also appending a C-terminal 6xHis purification tag'. The Sprints page says 'Our ordered constructs append CATCATCATCATCATCAT directly after the mature peptide, so the tag sits on exactly that carboxylate'. A judge reading the cluster in order meets three answers. Say here what the ordered construct carries and when it changed, and correct the other two pages. The verb is also doing you no favours: 'informed the decision' leaves the loop open where 'we moved' closes it.
